children: Factorial Funds, a venture firm launched five years ago by former Cruise engineer Sol Bier, has crossed $1 billion in realized profits, according to a letter the firm is sharing with its investors.
Most of Factorial's proceeds are in the form of SpaceX shares that were recently released from their post-initial public offering lockup, according to a person familiar with the situation.

The firm's distributions to its limited partners now total $965 million, according to the letter, with practically all of it coming from investments it made between 2022 and 2024 across multiple special-purpose vehicles. Factorial pocketed the remainder of the roughly $1 billion in proceeds.
The gross value of all of its investments, including distributed and paper gains, stood at more than $5 billion, according to the firm's estimates, as of August, the letter said.
Factorial Funds' success is an indication of broader liquidity finally coming to the venture market, due to a surge in IPOs and acquisitions.

That's a welcome relief after a long dry period that spooked limited partners and introduced fundraising challenges for managers. Still, the liquidity wave is likely to benefit a small number of venture fund managers, rather than the asset class as a whole.

In Factorial's case, the speed to such significant liquidity is highly unusual in the venture market. The San Francisco firm started investing in 2021 after Bier left Cruise, a self-driving car startup that was acquired and later folded by General Motors.

Bier at first raised large deal-by-deal SPVs instead of a standard venture fund. The firm aggregated those SPVs into what it calls Factorial Fund I, totaling $135 million in contributions. That pool generated 7.1 times of distributions-to-paid-in capital, according to the letter.

Only 17% of venture funds of the 2022 vintage had generated even a dollar of distributions as of the first quarter of this year, according to data from private-markets software company Carta. The median DPI for a 2022 vintage venture fund was zero, Carta said.

Factorial invested a total of roughly $80 million across separate deals in Elon Musk's xAI and SpaceX when they were private companies, the person said. Earlier this year, SpaceX acquired xAI, and then the combined company went public in the largest-ever IPO in June. Factorial still has restricted shares of SpaceX that it will get hold of later on, the person said.

More liquidity is likely in the offing for Factorial and others, given that Anthropic is expected to go public this fall. Factorial invested in the AI company's Series C round in 2023, at a valuation below $5 billion. Anthropic raised capital at a $965 billion valuation in May. Anthropic is Factorial's largest position, the person said.
The firm's portfolio also includes defense company Anduril Industries, AI startup Perplexity, AI voice company ElevenLabs and semiconductor chips business Fractile.

Factorial Funds has so far deployed about $500 million of the $750 million it has raised, including through a second, standard venture fund closed last year. Hyundai Motor Co. and Kia Corp. were anchor investors in the second fund, according to a press statement at the time.
Factorial will continue investing in artificial intelligence and infrastructure, and invest resources into research, according to the letter it shared with LPs.
